subject: Discovery recap: latency vs cost tradeoffs for triage model
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Caldwell <emma@nimblecare.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: latency vs cost tradeoffs for triage model

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our conversation so we’re aligned and can scope a short pilot: 

Pain points you called out
- Unit economics: current model spend spikes unpredictably during peak clinic hours; looking to reduce per-inference cost by ~50–70% to make real-time triage profitable.
- Latency sensitivity: patient-facing triage must feel instantaneous; you mentioned p95 <= 350ms as a workable target, but we discussed trying for p95 < 300ms for best UX.
- Quality tolerance: high sensitivity to hallucination on medication questions — cannot degrade clinically relevant outputs.

Current stack
- Frontend: React app w/ short-turn API calls to a Python service.
- Model: currently using a hosted chat endpoint (third-party API) with occasional on-prem GPU for batch jobs.
- Traffic: rough peak estimate ~200 req/s, ~20k DAU (Emma — please confirm volume).

Success criteria (what would make a pilot useful)
1) Maintain clinical-quality output (no material uptick in hallucinations measured by your prompt set).
2) Achieve p95 latency < 300ms for single-turn triage calls under expected production load.
3) Reduce per-inference cost by at least 50% vs your current provider at pilot scale.

Openness to optimizations
- You indicated batching is acceptable for background tasks but limited for live triage.
- You’re open to quantization (INT8) as long as we validate output quality.
- Caching: you liked the idea of short prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (session-based caching keyed by patient/session id).

Proposed next steps
1) Exchange a small sample payload + traffic profile (we can use the traffic_profile_q2.xlsx you mentioned).
2) Redwood runs a 1-week benchmark: defined prompt set, simulated traffic (200 req/s peak), and two model variants (fp16 baseline + int8 quantized).
3) Joint quality review at end of week with your ML team.
4) Pilot agreement (2–4 weeks of scoped traffic) if benchmarks meet success criteria.

I’ve attached a short pilot plan and a batching/caching primer to show how we approach unit economics without sacrificing latency (redwood-pilot-plan.pdf, redwood-batching-guide.pdf).

Are you available Wed 6/16 10–11am PT to kick off the pilot scoping call? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and loop in our bench team.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-pilot-plan.pdf (pilot scope + metrics), redwood-batching-guide.pdf (approach to batching/caching)

From: Emma Caldwell <emma@nimblecare.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: latency vs cost tradeoffs for triage model

Thanks Lauren — super helpful summary. A few clarifications and notes from our side: 

- Volume: confirmed — roughly 18k–22k DAU depending on marketing pushes; peak sessions ~180–220 req/s for short windows (10–15min).
- Latency: we prefer p95 <= 350ms as acceptable, but I agree aiming for <300ms would be ideal. For background reprocessing (nightly jobs) batching is fine; for live triage we can’t batch beyond micro-batching (2–4 requests) without hurting UX.
- Quantization: we’re open to INT8 for cost reasons but we will require a quality delta report against 100 clinical prompts (we have a test set).
- Security: we need to confirm data residency — PHI flows through the service, so any pilot must use our VPC or a redwood private deployment.

I attached our traffic profile workbook (traffic_profile_q2.xlsx) and the clinical prompt set link (shared in a separate email from my ML lead).

Wed 6/16 10–11am PT works for me — please include anyone needed from your bench/infra team. Also pls share an NDA if required; we can sign quickly.

—Emma
Emma Caldwell
Director, ML Ops | Nimbus Health
emma.caldwell@nimblecare.com | (617) 555-0147

Attachment: traffic_profile_q2.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Caldwell <emma@nimblecare.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: latency vs cost tradeoffs for triage model

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Emma. Looping in Aditya (solutions) and Marissa (CS) to confirm pilot logistics and security checklist. 

We’ll do the following before the Wed call:
- Redwood to provision a private pilot environment (VPC) and share an access checklist (Marissa will follow up with details).
- Bench: we’ll run three configurations during the 1-week benchmark:
  1) fp16 baseline (closest to your current provider)
  2) int8 quantized (aggressive cost win)
  3) int8 + prefix/KV caching (to test query reuse without increasing p95)
- We’ll capture: latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/inference, and hallucination rate on your 100-prompt clinical set.

Attachments included: redwood-pilot-plan.pdf (detailed steps & metrics) and redwood-batching-guide.pdf (implementation options).

I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 6/16 10am PT with a short agenda (15m bench intro, 30m pilot scoping). If you want us to include a draft pilot statement of work or mutual action plan ahead of the call, let me know — we can attach a one-page SOW.

Aditya/Marissa — can you confirm who will own the VPC onboarding checklist and the initial benchmark run?

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Lauren
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-pilot-plan.pdf, redwood-batching-guide.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Caldwell <emma@nimblecare.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: latency vs cost tradeoffs for triage model

Morning team — quick note from infra/bench side.

We’ve reserved bench capacity for the week of 6/22 to run the three configs Lauren outlined. To help us hit your p95 target while testing cost, could you share:
- a sample of your typical request payloads (anonymized) and the clinical prompt set link (we’ll match inputs exactly),
- expected concurrency profile (a one-hour window with per-second request counts) — the traffic_profile_q2.xlsx helps but a per-second CSV is ideal.

I’ve kicked off a short benchmark doc and uploaded an initial micro-benchmark run to Drive: https://drive.google.com/benchmark-5873 — that contains baseline fp16 numbers on an A100-like instance. We’ll extend this to int8 and caching configs once we have your sample payloads.

Marissa — think you can own the VPC onboarding checklist and coordinate credentials? I’ll take point on bench runs and produce the cost delta report (tokens/inference + $/1k requests).

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
